neutral_facts.value: The accused entered the house of the victim at midnight. A scuffle ensued between the accused and the victim, during which the accused stabbed the victim in the abdomen and thighs. The victim, who was a physically strong individual, managed to pin the accused to the ground. The accused then used a knife to stab the victim, causing fatal injuries. The accused also inflicted injuries on other witnesses present at the scene and threatened them with dire consequences. The accused were apprehended by the neighbours and handed over to the police. The victim succumbed to his injuries after being taken to the hospital.

appeal_history.value: Trial court: Convicted under Sections 302/34, 460 and 324 of the Indian Penal Code; High Court: Converted conviction under Section 302 to Section 304 Part I; Supreme Court: Set aside High Court's judgment and restored trial court's judgment

quotes.text: The trial court relying on the evidence of the aforesaid witnesses as supported by the medical evidence convicted and sentenced the accused under Sections 302/34, 460 and 324 of the Indian Penal Code
The High Court has been influenced by the fact that there was no common intention on the part of the accused to commit murder

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the two accused, who were armed, entered the house of the victims at midnight with the intention of committing robbery. They caused fatal injuries to the deceased and also injured other witnesses, which indicates a clear intention to cause death.

quotes.text: It cannot be ignored that the two accused, duly armed, had entered the premises at mid night with the intention of committing robbery
They were also charged with the offence punishable under Section 460

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was no common intention on the part of the accused to commit murder. They claimed that the deceased's death was an unfortunate accident resulting from the accused's attempt to extricate themselves from the deceased's grip during a scuffle.

quotes.text: The High Court has been influenced by the fact that there was no common intention on the part of the accused to commit murder
In these circumstances, the offence committed by A-2 comes within the purview of Section 304 I

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the common intention to commit murder can be inferred from the circumstances of the case, even if it arises during an incident, and that the initial purpose of robbery does not preclude the intention to cause death if the accused used weapons effectively.

quotes.text: The common intention can be inferred from the circumstances of the case and that the intention can be gathered from the circumstances as they arise even during an incident
The initial purpose was to commit robbery, but as the accused were armed with knives which they had used repeatedly and effectively, they were willing to kill

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the High Court's observation that the matter fell under Section 304 Part I and not Section 302 of the IPC was found to be erroneous. The trial court's conviction under Sections 302/34, 460 and 324 was restored.

quotes.text: The High Court's observation that the matter fell under Section 304 Part I and not under Section 302 of the IPC is erroneous
The High Court's judgment is set aside - The judgment of the trial court is restored
